validity.researcher_notes: P1911 'UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56 2' is the '2' twin of P1910 'UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56'. Both rows describe the IDENTICAL kilometer-post span (km0 -> km56) of the same physical trunk line, identical length 56 km, differing ONLY in recorded diameter (P1910 = 48 in, P1911 = 40 in). The parent asset is REAL and independently confirmed: UBTG-1 = 'Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk Gas' line, a Saudi Aramco Master Gas System pipeline. C.A.T. GROUP project page (Aramco contract 6600019233) states verbatim '2 No. of 56" gas Pipelines: SRG-2 (56 KM) and UBTG-1 (57 KM)', giving UBTG-1 ~57 km at 56 in diameter; JPT/SPE corroborates the MGS expansion context. HOWEVER, no independent source attests the per-segment km0->km56 decomposition or the 40 in diameter of THIS row. The only citations on the gem.wiki page are OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 (p.75) and 2017 (p.136) -- OPEC ASB is country-level production/reserves statistics and does NOT contain pipeline-segment, km-post, or per-segment diameter data, so those citations do not support this row's existence as a distinct entity or its diameter. The km0/km56 segment naming and the '2' suffix are hallmarks of a GIS/segment-table import where one trunk line was split into multiple endpoint-named rows, with parallel-diameter entries (40/48/56 in) double-counting the same right-of-way. Verdict 'concern/duplicate': P1911 most likely is not a separate physical pipeline from P1910 but the same km0->km56 span re-entered with a different diameter.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify diameter: independent source gives UBTG-1 as a 56-inch line, GEM records P1911 at 40 inches with no independent support.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records P1911 diameter = 40 in. The only independent attestation of UBTG-1 dimensions (C.A.T. GROUP, Aramco contract 6600019233) describes UBTG-1 as a 56-inch line ('2 No. of 56" gas Pipelines: SRG-2 ... and UBTG-1'). GEM's sibling segment rows split the same trunk into 48 in (P1910), 40 in (P1911), and 56 in (P1912, Hawiyah-UBTG-1-km0). The 40 in figure for this segment is not corroborated by any independent source and conflicts with the only independent diameter value found (56 in). Length (56 km) is roughly consistent with the independent ~57 km figure and is the one spec with partial support. Owner = Saudi Aramco is consistent with the Aramco MGS attribution. Fuel = Gas confirmed (UBTG = Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk GAS; part of the dry/sales-gas Master Gas System). Do not silently pass the 40 in diameter.

fills.researcher_notes: Fuel = Gas confirmed: UBTG-1 is a sales/dry gas pipeline in Saudi Aramco's Master Gas System (C.A.T. GROUP names it 'UBTG-1 Sales Gas Project', a 56-inch gas pipeline under Aramco contract 6600019233).

Country = Saudi Arabia confirmed: UBTG-1 (Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk Gas) is a Saudi Aramco Master Gas System line in Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia. Specific km0/km56 endpoint detail remains GEM-internal and unverified; left blank rather than fabricated.

Status = operating not independently confirmable for this specific km0->km56 '2' segment. The parent UBTG-1 trunk is an established/operating MGS line (built-out 1980s, ongoing MGS upgrades), but the C.A.T. GROUP / JPT sources describe an MGS *expansion* project (new SRG-2 + UBTG-1 sales-gas work), which could indicate construction-era activity rather than confirming this exact row as long-operating. No standalone source pins this segment's operational status; left UNRESOLVED rather than cite a non-corroborating page.

summary: P1911 parent asset (UBTG-1 Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk Gas) is real & Aramco-owned, but the row is a likely segment double-count of P1910 (identical km0->km56 / 56 km, only diameter differs 40 vs 48 in) and its 40-in diameter conflicts with the only independent figure (56 in); gem.wiki cites only OPEC ASB which lacks segment data.
